children: The Reserve Bank of Australia has clearly grown very uneasy about inflation risks, and data next week are expected to show why. Taylor Nugent, an economist at National Australia Bank, expects headline inflation to bounce higher to 4.1% in August on higher fuel prices, from 3.5% in July. In quarterly terms, trimmed mean inflation is tracking higher than the RBA's August forecast of 0.83%, he adds. NAB is forecasting a 1.0% on-quarter trimmed mean outcome, with the risk skewed to a 1.1% result, he says. Significant uncertainty remains about the path forward for energy costs, but the cost shock already realized is very large, Nugent says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
